title: India Draw 2-2 With China in Women's Hockey World Cup 2026 Opener
excerpt: Navneet Kaur's brilliant field goal and Deepika's penalty corner conversion helped India recover twice against China in their Pool D match at the Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen.
body:
• India drew 2-2 with China in their opening Pool D match at the FIH Women's Hockey World Cup 2026 in Amstelveen, Netherlands.
  • Navneet Kaur gave India an early lead with a field goal in the 8th minute before China equalised through a penalty stroke by Zhang in the 15th minute.
  • Deepika restored India's lead from a penalty corner in the 25th minute, but Ma levelled again for China from a penalty corner in the 39th minute.
  • India were reduced to 10 players during the match but held on for the draw in the tournament held at Wagener Stadium.

India's Strong Start

The Indian women's hockey team opened their FIH Hockey World Cup 2026 campaign with a hard-fought 2-2 draw against China in Pool D at the Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen, Netherlands, on Saturday.

India came out with attacking intent from the start. Navneet Kaur produced a sensational field goal in the 8th minute to give the team an early advantage. The forward's clinical finish showcased the kind of incisive attacking play that head coach Janneke Schopman has been building towards ahead of this tournament.

China Fight Back

China responded quickly. Zhang converted a penalty stroke in the 15th minute to level the scores at 1-1 heading into the break. The Chinese side, who qualified for the tournament through their Asia Cup victory, showed composure under pressure and refused to let India build on the early momentum.

India regrouped and Deepika struck from a penalty corner in the 25th minute to restore the lead at 2-1. The drag-flick specialist's precise execution gave the Indian dugout reason for optimism.

India Reduced to 10 Players

The match took a dramatic turn when India were reduced to 10 players. Despite the numerical disadvantage, the team fought to maintain their lead. However, China capitalised on the extra space and Ma converted a penalty corner in the 39th minute to make it 2-2.

The fourth quarter saw both teams push for a winner, but the defences held firm and the match ended in a draw.

Tournament Context

The Women's Hockey World Cup 2026 is being co-hosted by Belgium and the Netherlands, running from August 15 to 30. India are placed in Pool D alongside China, England, South Africa, and Bangladesh.

The World Cup returns to a special stage for Indian hockey. The women's team has been on an upward trajectory since their historic fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics, and this tournament represents another opportunity to establish India as a global force in women's hockey.

What's Next for India

India will next face a crucial Pool D match on August 18 as they look to build on this result. A win in the next game would put the team in a strong position to advance from the group stage. The team will need to convert their attacking chances more efficiently and maintain defensive discipline when reduced in numbers.
